newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian govt sees Independent satisfied.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian govt sees Independent satisfied.

text.p: Australian Government Senate Leader Robert Hill said on Thursday he expected to be able satisfy a demand by key Independent senator Brian Harradine in relation to the government's planned privatisation of Telstra Corp.

"Unless there is something further that I don't understand yet from Senator Harradine -- but no doubt we will learn as the debate progresses -- I'm sure that what he is seeking will be accommodated because it is not only fair and reasonable but it's also within the purpose and objectives of what we're seeking to do," Hill told Australian Broadcasting Corp.
Harradine has said he would like his home state of Tasmania to benefit from the environmental fund that the government promises to create if the planned sale of a third of Telstra goes ahead.
While the government is two votes short of a majority in the Senate, all but two senators have declared opposition to the privatisation, which requires a bill currently before the Senate.
Harradine and another Independent, Mal Colston, are the two senators who have not declared opposition and therefore represent the government's only hope of getting the bill passed.
Colston wants guarantees on Telstra employing people in his state, Queensland.
The government estimates that one-third of Telstra is worth about A$8 billion.
